Attorney here.

Under the common law, which most States still follow, there is no legal duty owed to render aid to a third party. So not stopping another person from walking into traffic falls under the common law. Obviously, one may feel a moral obligation to render aid, but that's different than a legal obligation.

However, there are situations where a duty is owed, such as a parent to the child. In the case where a duty is owed, then it is illegal to passively allow the ward to die. There can be defenses to that duty as well, such as in cases where the guardian is highly likely to die in the rescue attempt. The subject is very nuanced and often depends on what can or cannot be proven.

Well, in case of a parent, then until their child is more or less independent of their parents (I don't mean "adult", but "old enough to feed itself and take care of its most basic needs, given the resources"), then child's death as a result of neglect is manslaughter.
